title: Agri Land Sale: Understanding Tax Exemption Rules

faq.q: Is all agricultural land exempt from capital gains tax?
faq.a: No, only rural agricultural land is exempt from capital gains tax. Urban agricultural land is considered a capital asset and its sale is subject to capital gains tax.

faq.q: How is "urban" agricultural land defined for tax purposes?
faq.a: Agricultural land is considered urban if it falls within specific distances from a municipality or cantonment board, depending on the population of that area (e.g., within 2 km for population 10,000-1 lakh, 6 km for 1-10 lakhs, 8 km for over 10 lakhs).

faq.q: Can I claim Section 54F exemption if I sell rural agricultural land?
faq.a: No, Section 54F exemption is for Long-Term Capital Gains arising from the sale of *any* long-term capital asset other than a residential house. Since rural agricultural land is not considered a capital asset, its sale does not generate capital gains, and thus Section 54F is not applicable.

faq.q: What if I don't reinvest the entire sale proceeds under Section 54F?
faq.a: If you reinvest only a portion of the net sale consideration from urban agricultural land, the exemption under Section 54F will be proportionate to the amount reinvested. The remaining capital gains will be taxable.

faq.q: What is the Capital Gains Accounts Scheme?
faq.a: The Capital Gains Accounts Scheme (CGAS) allows taxpayers to deposit the unutilised amount of capital gains (or net sale consideration for Section 54F) into a designated account before the income tax filing deadline, if they haven't yet purchased or constructed the new asset. This ensures the exemption is claimed, and they have additional time to utilise the funds.

faq.q: Do NRIs also get these tax exemptions on agricultural land sales?
faq.a: Yes, the tax provisions for agricultural land sales, including the definition of rural vs. urban land and exemptions like Section 54F, apply equally to Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) as they do to resident Indians.

faq.q: What documents are needed to prove agricultural activity?
faq.a: Documents like land revenue records (e.g., 7/12 extract or similar state-specific documents), records of crop cultivation, evidence of agricultural income, or certificates from local agricultural departments can serve as proof of agricultural activity.
